[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"AWS CodeBuild: Continuous Integration Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy. CodeBuild eliminates the need to provision, manage, and scale your own build servers. It continuously scales and processes multiple builds concurrently, so your builds are not left waiting in a queue."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"An AWS account with appropriate permissions to create and manage CodeBuild projects, IAM roles, and S3 buckets."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Source code stored in a repository such as AWS CodeCommit, GitHub, or Bitbucket."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Create an IAM Role for CodeBuild"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"CodeBuild needs permissions to access your source code and other AWS resources. Create an IAM role with the necessary permissions."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to the IAM console in the AWS Management Console."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Create a new role. Choose 'AWS service' as the trusted entity and 'CodeBuild' as the service that will use this role."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Attach the 'AWSCodeBuildAdminAccess' policy or create a custom policy with the required permissions (e.g., access to S3 buckets, CodeCommit repositories)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Name the role (e.g., 'CodeBuildRole') and create it."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Create a CodeBuild Project"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"A CodeBuild project defines how CodeBuild will build your application."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to the CodeBuild console in the AWS Management Console."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Create build project'."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enter a project name (e.g., 'my-sample-project')."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the source: Select your source provider (e.g., 'GitHub', 'AWS CodeCommit', 'S3'). Provide the repository URL or bucket name."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the environment: Choose an environment image. You can use a managed image or a custom image from Docker Hub or ECR. Select the operating system, runtime, and image version. Choose an environment type (e.g., 'Linux', 'Windows', 'Arm')."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the buildspec: Choose 'Use a buildspec file' or 'Insert build commands'. A buildspec file is a YAML file that defines the build commands. If you choose to insert build commands, you can directly enter the commands in the console."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"Example buildspec.yml:

version: 0.2

phases:
  install:
    commands:
      - echo "Installing dependencies..."
      - npm install
  build:
    commands:
      - echo "Building the application..."
      - npm run build
  post_build:
    commands:
      - echo "Build completed. Running tests..."
      - npm run test
artifacts:
  files:
    - '**/*'
  discard-paths: yes
  base-directory: dist"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure artifacts: Specify where CodeBuild should store the build output. You can store it in an S3 bucket."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure service role: Select the IAM role you created in Step 1."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Create build project'."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Start a Build"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the project is created, you can start a build."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the CodeBuild console, select your project."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Start build'."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"You can choose to override the source version or use the default."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click 'Start build' again to confirm."},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Monitor the Build"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can monitor the build progress in the CodeBuild console."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The console displays the build status, logs, and artifacts."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"You can view the build logs in real-time to troubleshoot any issues."},{"order":34,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Automate Builds with Webhooks"},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can configure webhooks to automatically trigger builds when changes are pushed to your source repository."},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the CodeBuild console, select your project."},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Go to the 'Triggers' section."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable the webhook and configure the events that should trigger a build (e.g., 'Push', 'Pull request created')."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"For GitHub, you may need to configure the webhook in your GitHub repository settings as well."},{"order":40,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic overview of how to use AWS CodeBuild for continuous integration. You can further customize your CodeBuild projects to meet your specific needs, such as integrating with other AWS services like CodePipeline and CloudFormation."}]
